theorem_title: The successor iterate applies the transition once more
natural_language_statement:
For any type $X$, function $f:X\to X$, element $x\in X$, and $k\in\mathbb N$, let $f^k$ denote the source recursively defined iteration. Then

$$
f^{k+1}(x)=f(f^k(x)).
$$

This structural identity is inlined in the current publication plan; this leftover payload is not scheduled for upload.
formal_statement:
@[simp]
theorem NewMathDiscovery.RankedCoalescence.iterate_succ {α : Type} (f : α → α) (k : Nat) (x : α) :
    iterate f (k + 1) x = f (iterate f k x) := by sorry
